## Chinese
### 微型電腦淺說
**大頭 B**
朋友,你有沒有想過擁有一部電腦 ?你可以安坐家中,慢慢地撰寫電腦程 序,茶餘飯後,又可以玩「太空侵者 」,甚至印出自己的求職信、文件或情 信。在十年前,這一切都可說是夢想, 但現在的微型電腦,不祇可以將你的工 作順利地做完,而且可以為你控制家中 的電器操作。 
#### 微型電腦系統 
微型電腦的心臟是微型處理器,它 是集積電路的成品,體積極小,功用是 制整個系統的程序及執行各種指令和數 學邏輯運算。輔助的記憶系統方面主要 分兩大類:半導體記憶及磁性記憶。而記 憶的容量通常用字節〔 (Byte) 一個八 位數字組成的單元叫做字節來紀錄 普通的微型電腦有兩種記憶,一種叫做 祇讀存儲器(Read Only Memory ROM),它的功能是引導系統程序及 監察程序,這些存儲器所藏的資料是固 定及不會因為電流中斷時失去的,在普 通運算的情况下,也不能改寫這些資料 ,微型電腦的BASIC (註一)語言的 編譯程序通常是存在這些存儲器中。市 面上流行的微型電腦通常有4K 至 18k Bytes 的 ROM。(IK Bytes = 1028 Bytes)。另外一種的記憶叫做隨機存 取器(RAM 或 Random Access Memory) 它們是記憶數據及程序的單 位,記存的資料,亦會因電流中斷而消 失。微型電 中心記憶,通常在 128 K Bytes 以下,16K至64K Bytes 的微型電腦也最受歡迎,因為價格並不算高。
若要處理及存儲大量資料,玩家可 以用磁碟推進器(disk drive)或普 通的錄音機,它們主要分別是閱讀資料 的方法,磁碟推進器是用隨機存取的方 法(直接到任何磁道中的任何區段去存 取)這方法比用盒式磁帶的錄音機快捷 很多。 
微型電腦常用的磁碟是軟性的,安 放在硬紙壳內,以防止變形,這些軟磁 碟的尺寸,直徑為8英寸及5英寸兩 種,將來可能會有一些3 英寸的小型 磁碟面世。訊息是以許多磁脉冲序列的 形式存放在光滑的磁性表面上,這些訊 息通過磁性讀及寫來讀出或寫入。而在 盒式磁帶中,訊息有兩種不同的方法儲 存用數字或聲音,第一個方法可存大量 的數據,並能更快地對數據進行讀寫, 但也需要使用昂貴的磁帶部件。 
大部份廉價的印字機是以點陣的方 式來打印字符的(Dot Matrix Printers)。最簡單的點陣打印機所打印的 字符是由5×7點陣所組成,這些打印 機的平均速度為每秒鐘二十至幾百個字 符。某些便宜的非擊打式打印機使用一 種特殊的熱敏紙,這些印字機通常稱為 熱印打機。若果要處理文件或信件,最 好是用菊花輪式打印機(Daisy whoeel Printer)。 這種印字機的打印 部份,好像一朵菊花,而每個「花瓣」 的主端都有一個字符,它的優點是能印 出非常美觀的字符,典型打印速度為每 秒三十至五十個字符,但價錢比普通印 字機為貴,通常在一萬元以上。
有些廠家,更推出一些用 BASIC 的口袋型電算機,體積和普通的電算機 相同,而記憶也有1K以上,這些口袋 型電腦,可接駁錄音機和小型印字機全 套的售價不過二千元。 這一代日本出產的微型電腦,在功 能上都有很大突破,最近某公司推出的 微型電腦,就由兩隻微型處理器構成, 而且還有數千個漢字。記憶系統是用先 進的磁泡記憶系統。 總之,現代電子科技的突破性發展 意味着電腦在這十年之內有重大的改 變,影响到社會中每一階層及行業。
#### 如何購買 微型電腦
購買微型電腦,主要考慮的問題是 用途,個人需求及金錢限制,普通一部 微型電腦的售價由數百至數萬元不等, 若是資金不足,最好是選擇一些可以將 逐件附件配上的系統,因為有內置磁碟 推動器的電腦,價錢大多在一萬元以上 軟件也是一個極重要的因素,現今的 美國電腦有較完善或較易找到的軟件, 無論在遊戲,教育,商業及家庭方面的 的軟件供應齊全,日本電腦方面,遊戲 的軟件也許多,但其它有用的大多是用 日語寫成,所以在閱讀及理解這些軟件 時會有頗大的困難。
另一些選擇因素是電腦程序的語言 ,有一些電腦,是要經過裝配頗昂貴的 硬件(通常叫 Software Card)還要 加上磁碟及其推動器,才能使用某些程 序語言,如Fortran、Cobol等。但另 外幾 需要磁碟及推進器便行。 
如果你想打太空怪獸,和電腦下棋 ,不妨買一些有彩色監察器或可接駁彩 色電視機的電腦,但通常的解像力會很 低,若要提高影像質素,非要加添高解 像板及購買一部高解像的監察器不可, 但價錢驚人,應用在工商業或教育的電 腦,多是一些綠色或黑白的監察器,因 為它們解像力較高,價錢便宜,而且長 期使用也不會使人感到疲倦。 
發燒友可以在市面買一些電腦的線 路板及集成電路切合電腦,加上鍵盤便 可以操作了。鍵盤最好是要標準打字機 型及具有ASCII 與消除抖動功能的字 鍵(debouncis keys)。若要減少系 統所佔的空間,可以考慮九吋以下的監 察器,它們價錢不會貴,體積也很少 。至於磁碟推進器方面,可以買一些沒 有機壳及變壓器的。這樣,大概花費八 千元左右,便有一個電腦系統。 
微型電腦硬件的售價在這幾年內下 跌了很多,而一些普通的軟件也很便宜 ,大家祇要費數千元便可以用這些電腦 來解決一些繁複的問題。將來的微型電 腦,肯定會成為生活的一部份。

#### translated by Grok 4.5
**A Brief Talk on Microcomputers**  
Big Head B
Friend, have you ever thought of owning a computer? You can install it at home, gradually improve computer programs; after tea and meals you can play “Space Invaders”; you can even print out your own job-application letters, documents or love letters. Ten years ago all this could only be called a dream, but today’s microcomputers can not only finish your work smoothly for you, they can also control the electrical appliances in your home.
**The Microcomputer System**
The heart of a microcomputer is the microprocessor. It is a finished product of micro-circuits, extremely small in size, and its function is to control the programs of the entire system and to execute various instructions and mathematical operations. As for the auxiliary memory systems, they are mainly divided into two large categories: semiconductor memory and magnetic memory. Memory capacity is usually recorded in bytes (a unit composed of eight binary digits is called a byte). Ordinary microcomputers have two kinds of memory. One is called Read Only Memory (ROM). Its function is to guide the system programs and monitoring programs. The data stored in these memories is fixed and will not be lost when the power is cut off; under ordinary operating conditions these data cannot be rewritten either. The compiler for the BASIC language (Note 1) of a microcomputer is usually stored in these memories. The popular microcomputers on the market usually have 4K to 16K Bytes of ROM (1K Bytes = 1024 Bytes). Another kind of memory is called Random Access Memory (RAM). They are the units that store data and programs; the stored data will also disappear when the power is cut off. The central memory of a microcomputer is usually below 128K Bytes; microcomputers of 16K to 64K Bytes are the most popular, because the price is not considered high.
If one wants to process and store large amounts of data, players can use a disk drive or an ordinary cassette recorder. Their main difference lies in the method of reading data: a disk drive uses the random-access method (going directly to any sector on any track to read or write). This method is much faster than a cassette-tape recorder.
The disks commonly used by microcomputers are soft; they are placed inside a hard cardboard shell to prevent deformation. These soft disks come in two sizes, 8 inches and 5¼ inches in diameter; in the future there may appear some 3½-inch mini-disks. Information is stored in the form of many magnetic domains arranged in sequence on the smooth magnetic surface; this information is read out or written in by magnetic reading and writing. On cassette tapes, information is stored by two different methods—digital or audio. The first method can store large amounts of data and can read and write data faster, but it also requires the use of expensive tape components.
Most inexpensive printers print characters by the dot-matrix method (Dot Matrix Printers). The simplest dot-matrix printers form characters with a 5×7 matrix; the average speed of these printers is from twenty to several hundred characters per second. Some cheap non-impact printers use a special heat-sensitive paper; these printers are usually called thermal printers. If one wants to handle documents or letters, it is best to use a daisy-wheel printer. The printing part of this kind of printer looks like a daisy; each “petal” tip carries a character. Its advantage is that it can print extremely beautiful characters; typical printing speed is thirty to fifty characters per second, but the price is higher than ordinary printers, usually above ten thousand dollars.
Some manufacturers have even brought out pocket-sized calculators that use BASIC. Their size is the same as ordinary calculators, and their memory is over 1K. These pocket computers can be connected to a cassette recorder and a small printer; the whole set sells for no more than two thousand dollars.
This generation of Japanese-made microcomputers has made great breakthroughs in function. Recently a certain company has released a microcomputer composed of two microprocessors, and it even has several dozen Chinese characters. The memory system uses the advanced magnetic-bubble memory system.
In short, the breakthrough developments in modern electronic technology mean that computers will undergo major changes within this decade, affecting every stratum and every trade in society.
**How to Buy a Microcomputer**
When buying a microcomputer the main considerations are purpose, personal needs and money limits. The selling price of an ordinary microcomputer ranges from a few hundred to several tens of thousands of dollars. If funds are insufficient, it is best to choose a system that allows you to add accessories piece by piece, because computers with built-in disk drives mostly cost more than ten thousand dollars. Software is also an extremely important factor. Nowadays American computers have more complete or more easily found software; whether for games, education, business or home use, the software supply is comprehensive. Japanese computers also have many game programs, but most other useful ones are written in Japanese, so reading and understanding these programs presents considerable difficulty.
Another selection factor is the computer’s programming language. Some computers require the installation of expensive extra hardware (usually called a Software Card) plus a disk and its drive before certain programming languages such as Fortran or Cobol can be used. Other models only need a disk and drive.
If you want to fight space monsters and play chess with the computer, you might as well buy a machine that has a colour monitor or can be connected to a colour television; but the resolution is usually low. To raise image quality you must add a high-resolution board and buy a high-resolution monitor, yet the price is astonishing. Computers used in industry, commerce or education mostly have green or black-and-white monitors, because their resolution is higher, the price is cheaper, and long-term use does not make people feel tired.
Enthusiasts can buy computer circuit boards and integrated circuits on the market, assemble them themselves, add a keyboard, and the machine can operate. The keyboard had best be the standard typewriter style and possess ASCII and debounce keys. To reduce the space occupied by the system one can consider a monitor under nine inches; their price is not expensive and the bulk is small. As for the disk drive, one can buy models without casing and transformer. In this way, spending about eight thousand dollars or so will give you a computer system.
The selling price of microcomputer hardware has fallen a great deal in these few years, and some ordinary software is also very cheap. Everyone only needs to spend a few thousand dollars to use these computers to solve some complicated problems. In the future the microcomputer will certainly become part of life.

## Chinese
### Gemini 2.5 Flash | Aug 2026 | Deconstruct
#### 解構主義與文本縫隙分析:
- **「微型」與昂貴代價的內在矛盾**：文本宣揚微型電腦普及與平民化，但細列的硬體與打印機成本（高達數千至上萬元）暴露了其作為早期中產或菁英專屬品的不對等門檻。
- **個人自主與系統限制的二元對立**：文章構想了「坐鎮家中控制一切」的個人權能，卻同時揭示使用者必須受限於特定ROM/RAM規格、軟體語言套件及美日進口軟體生態的被動依賴。
- **平實語氣下的科技決定論痕跡**：平實的「淺說」包裝著強烈的科技決定論，將「微型電腦必將成為生活一部分」作為不言而喻的未來，掩蓋了初期硬體失效率與技術門檻的荒謬落差。
